---
title: "Row-grouping using `FACET`"
---

The `FACET` clause allows you to split your data and display each group alongside a group label.
This technique is great for making structure in the data explicit.

::: {.callout-note}
This page is about the `TABULATE` usage of the `FACET` clause.
For the `VISUALISE` usage, see [this page](facet.qmd).
:::

## Clause syntax
The `FACET` syntax contains a number of subclauses.

```ggsql
FACET <column>, ...
  SETTING <parameter> => <value>, ...
```

## Column selection

```ggsql
<column>, ...
```

In `FACET`, one or more comma separated columns can be used to split the data.
The first `column` is mandatory, and subsequent columns add nesting levels.
If the columns contain missing `null` values, these are handled by the `missing` setting.

## Settings

```ggsql
SETTING <parameter> => <value>, ...
```

Facets take a typical `SETTING` clause with key-value pairs.
It currently takes the following parameters:

* `missing`: Determines what happens with `null` values in the grouping columns. Can be one of:
    * `'first'` Keep the rows with missing group values and display these on top of regular groups.
    * `'last'` (default) Keep the rows with missing group values and display these underneath regular groups.
    * `'drop'` Removes the rows with missing group values from the output table.
* `place`: Placement options of the group labels. One of the following:
   * `'top'` (default) Interleaves table body rows with group label rows. Group labels are placed above its member rows spanning all columns.
   * `'left'` Places group labels in the stub on the left. Group labels are vertically merged across member rows.


## Examples

Declare a facet column.

```{ggsql}
CREATE TEMP TABLE my_data AS 
SELECT DISTINCT ON (species, island, sex) * FROM ggsql:penguins

TABULATE * FROM my_data
  FACET sex
```

Omit missing group variables from the table.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
  FACET sex SETTING missing => 'drop'
```

Alternatively, missing group variables can be given a proper label using `FORMAT`.
Note that `missing => 'drop'` has priority over any relabeling in `FORMAT`.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
  FACET sex
  FORMAT sex RENAMING null => 'unknown'
```

Place grouping labels in the stub.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
  FACET sex SETTING place => 'left'
```

Using multiple group columns to group gives nested labels.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
  FACET species, island
```

When group labels are placed in the stub, the labels can be controlled by `LABEL`.

```{ggsql}
TABULATE * FROM my_data
  FACET species, island SETTING place => 'left'
  LABEL island => 'Place', species => 'Type'
```
